\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Invariance — Taylor}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.Taylor
\section{Overview}
Cubic Taylor approximation with an explicit fourth-order remainder gives integrability and scalar replacement estimates for the invariance moment conditions.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Cubic Taylor remainder bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_sub_taylor_cubic_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $\psi\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be $C^4$ and let $C\ge0$ satisfy $|\psi^{(4)}(t)|\le C$ for all real $t$. For all real $a,b$, $\left|\psi(a+b)-\sum_{j=0}^3\psi^{(j)}(a)b^j/j!\right|\le Cb^4/24$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Integrability under fourth-moment control]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_test_of_memLp_four}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_sub_taylor_cubic_le, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.integrable_mul_pow_of_memLp}
\difficulty{4}
Let $Z\in L^4(\mu)$ be real-valued on a probability space $(\Omega,\mu)$, and let $\psi\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be $C^4$. If some $C\ge0$ bounds $|\psi^{(4)}(t)|$ for every real $t$, then $\psi(Z)$ is integrable under $\mu$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Expected cubic polynomial for matched moments]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_taylor_cubic}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasInvarianceMoments, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.integrable_mul_pow_of_memLp}
\difficulty{4}
Let $X$ be a real input on a probability space, measurable up to a null set with finite fourth absolute moment, first three moments $0,1,0$, and fourth moment at most $9$. For any real function $\psi$ and real $a,b$, $\mathbb E[\sum_{j=0}^3\psi^{(j)}(a)(bX)^j/j!]=\psi(a)+\tfrac12\psi^{(2)}(a)b^2$. Here iterated differentiation assigns zero at a point where the derivative does not exist, so the identity requires no smoothness of $\psi$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Expected scalar Taylor error]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_integral_sub_taylor_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasInvarianceMoments, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_sub_taylor_cubic_le, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_test_of_memLp_four, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_taylor_cubic, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.integrable_mul_pow_of_memLp}
\difficulty{5}
Let $X$ be a real input on a probability space, measurable up to a null set with finite fourth absolute moment, first three moments $0,1,0$, and fourth moment at most $9$. Let $\psi\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be $C^4$ and let $C\ge0$ satisfy $|\psi^{(4)}(t)|\le C$ for all real $t$. For all real $a,b$, $|\mathbb E\psi(a+bX)-\psi(a)-\tfrac12\psi^{(2)}(a)b^2|\le(3C/8)b^4$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Comparison of scalar affine input laws]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.affine_replacement_bound}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasInvarianceMoments, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_integral_sub_taylor_le}
\difficulty{4}
Let $X$ and $Y$ be real inputs on possibly different probability spaces, each measurable up to a null set with finite fourth absolute moment, first three moments $0,1,0$, and fourth moment at most $9$. Let $\psi\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be $C^4$ and let $C\ge0$ satisfy $|\psi^{(4)}(t)|\le C$ for all real $t$. For every real $a,b$, $|\mathbb E\psi(a+bX)-\mathbb E\psi(a+bY)|\le(3C/4)b^4$.
\end{theorem}
